description: How digital hardware is described in Verilog, simulated with test benches, synthesised to gates and mapped onto an FPGA. Students write modules, verify them with self-checking test benches and finish by assembling a small processor.
modelledOn: Harris and Harris, Digital Design and Computer Architecture
Chu, FPGA Prototyping by Verilog Examples
Palnitkar, Verilog HDL: A Guide to Digital Design and Synthesis
outcomes: Write synthesisable Verilog for combinational and sequential circuits using structural, dataflow and behavioural styles.
Design finite state machines in HDL and choose a state encoding with a stated reason.
Build self-checking test benches and use waveforms to find and fix functional bugs.
Read synthesis and timing reports and close timing on a failing design by pipelining or restructuring.
Explain the FPGA fabric and map a design onto LUTs, block RAM, DSP slices and pins.
Implement, simulate and run a small processor from datapath and control unit descriptions.

units.title: Hardware description language fundamentals
topics: Why HDLs exist: simulation versus synthesis, Verilog versus VHDL, the design flow from RTL to bitstream
Modules, ports, wires and regs, vectors, and four-valued logic (0, 1, X, Z)
Literals, operators, bit-select, part-select and concatenation
Structural modelling with gate primitives and module instantiation; hierarchy
Dataflow modelling with continuous assignments; parameters and generate blocks

units.title: Combinational modelling
topics: assign statements and always @(*) blocks; sensitivity lists and their pitfalls
if/else and case statements; avoiding unintended latches and full-case coverage
Multiplexers, decoders, encoders and priority logic in HDL
Arithmetic in HDL: adders, subtractors, comparators and a parameterised ALU
Parameterised designs: generate-for loops for ripple adders and bit-slice arrays

units.title: Sequential modelling
topics: Clocked always blocks; blocking versus non-blocking assignment and race avoidance
D flip-flops with synchronous and asynchronous reset, and clock enable
Registers, shift registers and counters including modulo-N and up/down
Inferred memories: register files, ROM and RAM with synchronous read
Clock domain crossing: two-flip-flop synchronisers and metastability handling

units.title: Finite state machine design
topics: Moore and Mealy machines in HDL: one-, two- and three-process coding styles
State encoding: binary, Gray and one-hot, and their trade-offs on FPGAs
Worked designs: sequence detector, vending machine and traffic-light controller
Handshake protocols and a UART transmitter controller
Safe state machines: reset behaviour, unreachable states and glitch-free outputs

units.title: Simulation and test benches
topics: Event-driven simulation: simulation time, delta cycles and the scheduling regions
Test bench structure: clock and reset generation, initial blocks and stimulus
Self-checking test benches with $display, assertions and expected-output comparison
Waveform debugging, X propagation and common functional bugs
Verification planning: directed and random stimulus, golden reference models and coverage ideas

units.title: Synthesis and timing closure
topics: The synthesis flow: elaboration, logic optimisation and technology mapping
Inferred hardware, synthesisable subsets and common coding errors that break synthesis
Static timing analysis: setup and hold slack, critical path and clock skew
Timing constraints: clock period, input and output delay, false and multicycle paths
Closing timing: pipelining, retiming, logic duplication and resource sharing

units.title: FPGA architecture and toolflow
topics: Logic fabric: look-up tables, flip-flops, slices, carry chains and routing
Block RAM, DSP slices, clock managers and PLLs
Place and route, bitstream generation and device programming
Pin constraints, I/O standards and board bring-up with switches, LEDs and displays
Resource and power estimation; FPGA versus ASIC versus microcontroller trade-offs

units.title: Building a small processor on an FPGA
topics: Instruction set design for a 16-bit teaching processor: formats, registers and addressing modes
Datapath in HDL: ALU, register file, program counter and memory interface
Control unit as a state machine or microcode ROM
Loading programs, memory-mapped I/O and a UART or display peripheral
System integration: test programs, timing report, resource report and demonstration

schedule.title: From logic design to HDL
schedule.exercise: Write down the Verilog port list and internal signals for a 4-bit comparator, and say which values a 4-valued signal can hold and what each means.

tasks.title: Describe a 2-input AND gate as a Verilog module, build the same gate in the circuit bench and compare outputs for all four inputs
Evaluate ten Verilog expressions using concatenation, part-select and reduction operators by hand and confirm each result in the maths lab
Draw the design flow from RTL to bitstream as a diagram, labelling the file produced and the check performed at each stage

schedule.title: Structural and dataflow modelling
schedule.exercise: Write a full adder structurally from gate primitives and again with continuous assignments, then build a 4-bit adder by instantiating it four times.

tasks.title: Build the structural full adder from XOR, AND and OR gates and verify all eight input rows against the Verilog truth table
Instantiate four full adders into a 4-bit ripple adder, then check 30 chosen input pairs including carry-out cases
Write a script that generates the Verilog text of an N-bit ripple adder from a parameter and checks it for N equal to 4, 8 and 16

schedule.title: Describing combinational logic
schedule.exercise: Code a 4-to-1 multiplexer, a priority encoder and a 4-bit ALU with add, subtract, AND and OR, and mark where an incomplete case would create a latch.

tasks.title: Build a 4-to-1 multiplexer in the bench that matches your case-statement description and verify all select and data combinations
Fix a priority encoder description whose missing default branch infers a latch, then show in the bench that the output is purely combinational
Build a 4-bit ALU with flags matching a given HDL spec and verify 24 operand pairs, including overflow and zero results

schedule.title: Flip-flops, registers and memories in HDL
schedule.exercise: Write a clocked shift register and a modulo-12 counter with enable, explain the difference between blocking and non-blocking assignment, and sketch a 2-flip-flop synchroniser.

tasks.title: Build a D flip-flop with synchronous reset and enable and show in the timing view that reset acts only on the clock edge
Build a modulo-12 counter with enable and compare its waveform over 30 clock cycles with the behaviour of your HDL description
Model a swap of two registers with blocking and non-blocking semantics in code and show which one yields a correct exchange

schedule.title: Writing state machines in HDL
schedule.exercise: Code a 1011 overlapping sequence detector as a Mealy and a Moore machine and compare their state counts and output timing.

tasks.title: Step through a given Moore machine in the automata view with a 16-bit input and record the state after every clock
Implement the 1011 detector with overlap in the bench and test it on a 24-bit stream with four hidden occurrences
Build the same 6-state controller with binary and one-hot encoding, compare gate counts and output glitches, and state which you would use

schedule.title: Protocol controllers and safe FSMs
schedule.exercise: Draw the state diagram of a UART transmitter with start bit, eight data bits and stop bit, and list what happens if the FSM powers up in an illegal state.

tasks.title: Trace a ready/valid handshake between two small machines on a visualiser and mark the clock cycles in which a transfer occurs
Build a UART transmitter FSM that serialises the byte 0x4B at a divided baud clock and check the 10 line levels in the timing view
Add a recovery path to a 5-state one-hot machine so a forced illegal state returns to idle, and demonstrate it by injecting a fault

schedule.title: How simulators work and writing test benches
schedule.exercise: Trace the delta cycles of a small circuit with a combinational feedback chain, then outline a self-checking test bench for a 4-bit adder.

tasks.title: Step through event-driven simulation of three chained gates and record which signals update in each delta cycle
Write a test bench in code that generates a clock and reset, drives a counter model and prints the count for 20 cycles
Write a self-checking bench for an adder model that tests all 512 inputs against a reference and reports the first mismatch it finds

schedule.title: Debugging and verification planning
schedule.exercise: Given a waveform showing an X on an output after reset, find the uninitialised register and propose a fix, then list the corner cases for a 4-bit counter test plan.

tasks.title: Locate the signal responsible for an X on the output of a given circuit using the timing view and explain how it propagated
Generate 1,000 random operand pairs for an ALU model, compare against a reference and count how many corner cases they cover
Find and fix three injected bugs in a given FSM and counter design using waveforms alone, and write the test that would have caught each

schedule.title: Synthesis and static timing
schedule.exercise: Given a three-stage path with listed cell delays, compute setup slack at 100 MHz, then restructure the logic by pipelining so that it meets 200 MHz.

tasks.title: Read the critical path of a given circuit, add its gate delays and compute the maximum clock frequency by hand and in the timing view
Compute setup and hold slack for five paths with different skew and constraints, and plot slack against clock period
Insert a pipeline register in a failing 4-stage multiply-add path, verify equal results with one extra cycle of latency, and report the new frequency

schedule.title: Inside the FPGA fabric
schedule.exercise: Implement a 4-input function in a 4-input LUT by writing its 16-bit configuration, then explain how a carry chain speeds up an adder.

tasks.title: Fill in the 16-entry configuration table of a 4-input LUT for a given function and verify with the truth table tool
Map a 6-input function onto 4-input LUTs by Shannon decomposition and test all 64 input rows in the bench
Compare the cycle counts of a 16-tap filter built from LUT logic and from a DSP slice with a pipelined multiplier

schedule.title: Board bring-up and platform choices
schedule.exercise: Write the constraint lines that connect four switches, four LEDs and a clock pin of an FPGA board, and justify FPGA over a microcontroller for a 100 MHz sensor filter.

tasks.title: Wire a push-button and an LED to a board model with the correct pull-up and resistor and read the pin state in the monitor
Drive a 4-digit seven-segment display by multiplexing with a counter-based refresh and verify that no digit flickers at 1 kHz
Plot cost, power and latency of FPGA, microcontroller and ASIC options over production volume and choose one for a solar water-pump controller

schedule.title: Processor architecture and datapath
schedule.exercise: Define a 16-bit instruction format with eight instructions, then draw the datapath and write the control word for ADD and LOAD.

tasks.title: Decode six 16-bit instruction words by hand using the given format and check each against the assembly CPU visualiser
Build a datapath with eight registers, an ALU and a program counter, and execute a three-step ADD by setting the controls manually
Add a control FSM that sequences fetch, decode and execute for four instructions and verify a short program in the timing view

schedule.title: Running a program on your processor
schedule.exercise: Write a program that sums the numbers 1 to 10 and writes the result to a memory-mapped LED register, and list the resources and the worst slack from the reports.

tasks.title: Assemble and run a program summing 1 to 10 on the assembly CPU and record the register values after each loop pass
Map a processor output register to an LED bank and a switch bank as memory-mapped I/O and run a program that copies switches to LEDs
Run a 20-instruction test program on the full processor, trace pipeline-free execution, and report cycles per instruction and critical path
